items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: But I know Trum Boyd was playing, he was playing with Paul Whiteman.

ctx.x: So you got to know where all those rocks are. Yeah. How long were you with Faith Merrill?

From about, 1918 afternoon till about around 19. 19, 19, 19, I didn't work with Faith No More on the boat. But I worked on the boat and I went back on the boat with, uh- I worked on the boat with Dewey Jackson. I worked on the boat with Eddie Allen. I worked on the boat with, uh, Charlotte Craig. I worked on the island Queen too, or the Cincinnati. And the captain got all sorted with us. Man, we had the people screaming. And he said, Jesus Christ, you fell in a bunch of sticks. They got us screaming over there.…

items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: Because I played with the Trum Boy on, what's he called them? C Melody. C Melody. Yeah. Trum Boy. Bix was on piano then.

ctx.x: He was at the Arcade in 22. Because I'd run away with my first wife and I know I was in St. Louis. Maybe you were there for a week. Yeah, possibly. Because I know he was working with Charlie Strait. Was he good by 1922? Was he?

He was really fooling around more with the piano. Wait a minute. I think it was 21. 21 because the year before I left my first wife. Because I played with the Trum Boy on, what's he called them? C Melody. C Melody. Yeah. Trum Boy. Bix was on piano then.
Bix played piano. And then Pee Wee. And I never know who he was.
